title: Mangrove Forests Are Growing Back Worldwide
paragraphs: Mangroves are trees that grow in salty water near the coast. They protect the land from big waves. They also keep a lot of carbon.
Scientists looked at satellite pictures from 1984 to 2023. First, the world lost many mangroves. The loss was nearly 3,000 square kilometres until 2010.
After 2010, things changed. Mangroves grew again. They grew by nearly 2,000 square kilometres. This is good news, but the work is not finished.
